title: Indeliberate and deliberate motions
source_text: XXXI. Prioris generis motus, juxta ipsum, sunt indeliberati, & physice tantum non libere a facultatibus nostris eliciti: posterioris vero liberi sunt & deliberati. Ad prius genus pertinent piae cogitationes & pia desideria, absque nostro consensu immediate a Deo immissa: ad posterius vero, omnes virtutum Christianarum actus, quos Dei gratia juvante elicimus.
pass_a_gloss: XXXI. Motions of the former kind, according to him, are indeliberate, and only physically not freely elicited from our faculties: but of the latter are free and deliberate. To the former kind pertain pious thoughts and pious desires, sent in immediately by God without our consent: but to the latter, all the acts of Christian virtues, which by the help of God's grace we elicit.
pass_b_english: Thesis XXXI. According to him, the motions of the first kind are indeliberate: our faculties produce them only physically, not freely. Those of the second kind are free and deliberate.

The first kind covers devout thoughts and devout desires that God sends directly, without our consent. The second covers all the acts of the Christian virtues that we bring forth with the help of God's grace.
